name: Malchiram
overview: Malchiram was a male descendant from the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Jehoiachin, also known as Jeconiah. His lineage places him within the royal line of Judah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:18. Beyond his paternal connection, Scripture provides no additional personal details or notes about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Malchiram means '[my] king is exalted,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the acknowledgment of God's sovereignty. This proper name, found in 1 Chronicles 3:18, was not given directly by God but carries significance related to kingship and exaltation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Malchiram as the son of Jehoiachin, the king of Judah, situating him within a significant royal family. No other familial relationships are documented beyond this paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Malchiram's significance lies primarily in his place within the Davidic royal lineage, as a son of Jehoiachin, who was a key figure in the history of Judah's monarchy. His mention in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 3:18 underscores the continuity of God's covenant promises through the line of David. Although the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his inclusion affirms the preservation of the Messianic lineage through the tribe of Judah.
